title: Fig: Ancient Figs You Can Visit
meta_description: A genus too wide to trunk-measure: Okinawa's 300-year banyan, Rio's first landmarked tree, and one shielded yearly from a bonfire festival.
intro: A fig this size stops being a single trunk and becomes a structure. Nago's Hinpun Gajumaru is the clearest case: its aerial roots fused into a mass nearly 12 metres around, wide enough that no one measures a trunk at all, and old enough to have gradually swallowed a pine growing beside it, referenced in Ryukyuan poetry by the 1690s. Rio de Janeiro's fig on Rua Faro became the city's very first landmarked tree in 1980, and only after neighbours physically stood under it to stop a construction crew. Alicante's fig gets a gentler kind of protection: fireproof tarps wrapped around it every June before the plaza around it is set alight for the Fogueres festival, a shield that failed in 2026 and scorched part of its crown. None of the three has ever been keyed to an exact species, so each ships as Ficus sp. rather than a guess.
